learning: Compare directly with iteration 9. If the oval finish rate is at least 0.9 and slalom max_error falls below 0.06 m, y = 0.07 m is the new base. If the oval finish rate is below 0.8, return to y = 0.06 m. If s-bend oscillation rises well above 0.36 without finishes falling, the next controller step is kd damping, not sensing.
notes: Builder's forward row at y = 0.07 m with the iteration 9 controller unchanged. Only the sensor y position differs from iteration 9 (620.55), so any outcome change is attributable to the offset.
rationale: Iteration 9 (y = 0.06 m, kd 0.8) is the best raced design at 620.55. Oval finished 20 of 20, s-bend 17 of 20 with mean max_error 0.040 m, and slalom ended off-track in all 20 trials with mean max_error 0.066 m and progress 0.19. The Builder's proposed row moves to y = 0.07 m, with x and sensor size unchanged. The Builder's stated keep rule is an oval finish rate of at least 0.9 and slalom max_error below 0.06 m. I accept that rule and the fallback to y = 0.06 m if the oval finish rate drops below 0.8. I keep the iteration 9 controller exactly (kp 5.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.8, base_speed 1.2, last_direction, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]). The sensor x positions are unchanged, so the signal scale and weights still match the row, and the only variable under test is the forward offset. The forward step is expected to raise s-bend steering oscillation further (it rose from 0.27 to 0.36 between y = 0.04 and y = 0.06), so kd 0.8 is the damping most likely to be stressed. Slalom progress (0.19) is far from a finish, so I do not expect slalom completion in this race. The main risk is that the oval finish rate falls below 0.8 because the controller is tuned to y = 0.06 m, in which case the Builder's fallback applies.
